newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to redraft controversial health bills.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to redraft controversial health bills.

text.p: South Africa's Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma said on Wednesday she would withdraw and redraft three controversial health bills which have been fiercely opposed by the pharmaceutical industry and opposition politicians.
Zuma said in a statement to parliament that she had taken note of criticism during two days of public hearings.
"I would like to study the submissions and make sure that the genuine concerns and suggestions are taken on board. I will therefore re-submit the bills to cabinet next week," she said.
Opposition parties which walked out of the public hearings in protest against the rejection of their criticisms congratulated Zuma on her decision.
Two proposals from Zuma have particularly enraged the pharamceuticals industry.

The first aims to promote cheap generic substitutes over brand name drugs by instructing pharmacists to dispense them unless expressly forbidden to do so. The industry says that amounts to mandatory substitution.
The second measure would also curb brands by barring sales to the State of medicines containing the brand-name in the label.
